chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Isa ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) would not say Takbir in the two Eid prayers except with one Takbir, until his tongue was slow (with age), so Husayn (peace be upon him) would say it. Then, on one Eid day, his mother dressed him and sent him with his grandfather. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said Takbir, and Husayn (peace be upon him) said Takbir when the Prophet said it, seven times. Then he stood for the second time, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said Takbir, and Husayn (peace be upon him) said Takbir when he said it, five times. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) made it a Sunnah, and the Sunnah remained established until today.

key_terms.أبطأ عليه لسانه: His tongue became slow (due to age)
key_terms.العيدان: The two Eid prayers (Fitr and Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic tradition regarding the number of Takbirs in Eid prayers according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique role of Imam Husayn (AS) as a liturgical partner in Eid prayers, illustrating the transmission of ritual authority within the Ahl al-Bayt. The specific counts of seven and five Takbirs for the second and first Rak'ahs respectively are established here as a confirmed Sunnah, reflecting the Prophet's adaptation to his physical state while preserving the ritual's integrity through his grandson. This incident underscores the continuity of prophetic practice and the scholarly emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's direct involvement in establishing Islamic jurisprudence.
